title: Chewy vs. MercadoLibre: Which Consumer Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?
detail:

Does the stability of the pet category outweigh the high growth of Latin American e-commerce? Choosing between Chewy Inc. (NYSE:CHWY) and MercadoLibre Inc. (NASDAQ:MELI) requires balancing recurring revenue against regional market dominance.

Chewy focuses on the North American pet market through specialized fulfillment and a high-margin subscription model. MercadoLibre operates a massive integrated commerce and fintech ecosystem across 18 countries in Latin America. Investors often compare them to see if a niche leader or a geographic titan offers better long-term potential.

The case for Chewy

Chewy operates as a leading online retailer for pet owners, providing everything from food and toys to prescription medications. The company partners with approximately 4,000 brands and has developed its own private labels such as Frisco and American Journey. A significant portion of its business comes from the PracticeHub platform, which is currently used by roughly 50% of all veterinary clinics in the United States. This specialized focus among retail stocks allows the company to build deep loyalty through subscription-like programs.

In the 12 months ended Aug. 2, 2026, revenue reached about $13.1 billion. This represented growth of roughly 5.9% compared to the prior twelve-month period. Net income for the period was about $273.7 million, as the company continues to focus on improving profitability through its high-margin Autoship subscription service and pharmacy sales.

As of its February 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is approximately 1.0x, meaning total debt is equal to shareholder equity. The current ratio, which measures a company's ability to cover short-term debts with short-term assets, is roughly 0.9x. In the fiscal year ended Feb. 1, 2026, free cash flow was around $562.4 million. Note that for the fiscal year ended Feb. 1, 2026, stock-based compensation represented roughly 43.1% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since stock-based compensation is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

The case for MercadoLibre

MercadoLibre provides an integrated commerce and financial services ecosystem across 18 different countries in Latin America. Its Marketplace platform facilitates both direct sales and third-party transactions, supported by an extensive logistics network known as Mercado Envios. The company also operates Mercado Pago, a fintech powerhouse that handles online payments, credit, and asset management for millions of users. By combining these services, the company captures growth from both the rise of digital shopping and the increasing adoption of digital financial tools in emerging markets.

The 'Big Short' investor sold half of his Nvidia and VanEck Semiconductor ETF puts at a profit.

The trades come as Nvidia is set to drop for the seventh consecutive trading session.

Burry bought an additional 20% in MercadoLibre (MELI) and highlighted "absolute relative strength" in a few healthcare stocks.

The 'Big Short' famed investor Michael Burry locked in profits on half of his bearish bets against Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) and an ETF that tracks the semiconductor sector on Friday, capitalizing on a steep technology sell-off this week while maintaining a long-term bearish bet on the Nasdaq 100.

In a Friday update to subscribers of his 'Cassandra Unchained' Substack, Burry said he sold 50% of his put options on both Nvidia and the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH), locking in what he described as substantial gains while keeping the remaining half open. Put options gain value when the underlying shares decline.

Burry also pared back bullish exposure elsewhere, selling roughly one-third of his call options on animal health company Zoetis Inc. (ZTS) to secure profits. At the same time, he left his bearish April 2027 put options on the Nasdaq 100 completely untouched, signaling continued caution toward large-cap technology valuations.

Meanwhile, Burry boosted his stake in Latin American e-commerce giant MercadoLibre Inc. (MELI) by 20% and highlighted "absolute relative strength" in a few healthcare stocks like Molina Healthcare (MOH) and HCA Healthcare (HCA), as well as Photoshop maker Adobe (ADBE) and Sprouts Farmers Market (SFM).

NVDA Stock Set For Worst Week Since 2018

Burry's profit-taking coincided with a punishing week for Nvidia shares, which extended a seven-session losing streak on Friday. The chipmaker's stock was also on track to record its worst weekly performance since November 2018. The stock has been in constant turmoil ever since former CEO Jensen Huang accepted his romantic involvement with alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang.

A strong quarterly earnings print and a rosy outlook did little to prop up the share price of the chipmaker, which currently sits at the very top of the entire AI infrastructure buildout. Earlier this week, Nvidia reported that revenue more than doubled year-over-year to a record $115.8 billion, while net profit surged 109% to $64.9 billion, topping Wall Street forecasts. Interim CEO Colette Kress also guided fourth-quarter revenue to $130 billion and raised the company's fiscal 2028 revenue growth outlook to 75%.

Key Takeaways

A fund that manages $4.7 billion added to its stakes in MercadoLibre, Mastercard and Visa in the third quarter, according to its 13F.

MercadoLibre was the biggest of the three additions, and the stock is down 22% since Sept. 30 as its operating margin keeps shrinking.

Mastercard and Visa are up 14% and 12% since the quarter ended, and analysts' average targets for both are at their highs for the year.

Mastercard is the one the numbers back best, with estimates and targets rising and a multiple below its long-run average.

Route One Investment Company's newest 13F has one bet that's down 22% and two that are up by double digits.

The filing, for the quarter ended Sept. 30 and filed Nov. 16, shows the fund's three biggest additions were MercadoLibre (MELI:NASDAQ), Mastercard (MA:NYSE) and Visa (V:NYSE). The firm manages $4.7 billion in all, according to its latest Form ADV, and its 13F holds $2.33 billion of US stocks across 19 positions.

The biggest add is down 22%

The fund held 81,650 MercadoLibre shares on Sept. 30, 25% more than at June 30. They were worth $141 million, 6.0% of its 13F stocks and its ninth-largest position.

The stock has fallen 22% since. MercadoLibre's third-quarter revenue rose 45% to $10.75 billion, but its GAAP operating margin fell to 6.3% from 9.8% as it spent on free shipping, almost 20% more fulfillment space and affiliate marketing in Brazil.

Goldman Sachs cut its target to $2,100 from $2,230 on Nov. 11 and kept its Buy rating. The average target fell from about $2,850 a year ago to $2,153, its low for the year.

MercadoLibre (MELI): analysts' consensus (mean) price target, $ per share, last year (TIKR)

That's still 59% above the share price, with 25 analysts' targets running from $1,600 to $2,700.

TIKR tracks 25 analysts on MercadoLibre. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on MercadoLibre, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See MercadoLibre's Analyst Ratings

Mastercard is already up 14%

The two payment networks have gone the other way. The fund held 84,800 Mastercard shares on Sept. 30, 20% more than at June 30. They were worth $47 million, or 2.0% of its 13F stocks, and the stock has gained 14% since.

Mastercard's services revenue grew 19% in the third quarter, and its total revenue grew 14%. More than a dozen firms raised their targets after the report, J.P. Morgan to $755 from $720 among them. The average target has climbed from $657 a year ago to $721, its high for the year.

Mastercard (MA): analysts' consensus (mean) price target, $ per share, last year (TIKR)

That's 15% above the share price, from 40 analysts.

Visa is up 12%, but its banks want more

Visa's quarter looks a lot like Mastercard's, with one more worry. The fund held 128,700 Visa shares on Sept. 30, 21% more than at June 30. They were worth $46 million, or 2.0% of its 13F stocks, and the stock is up 12% since.

The worry is what Visa pays the banks that issue its cards. Visa guided to low-double-digit revenue growth for fiscal 2027, and its CFO flagged faster growth in client incentives. Freedom Broker cut Visa to Hold from Buy on Nov. 4, citing rising incentives and a record number of contract renewals. Cantor Fitzgerald went the other way, raising its target to $500 from $445, and the average has risen from $394 a year ago to $451, its high for the year.

Visa (V): analysts' consensus (mean) price target, $ per share, last year (TIKR)

That's 12% above the share price, from 40 analysts.

Do the numbers back the fund?

MercadoLibre looks cheapest. At about 31x forward earnings, it trades below even its 33x low at the end of March and far below its 48x average since 2023.

But the estimates behind that multiple keep shrinking. In September 2025, analysts expected $66.55 of normalized EPS for 2026, and now they expect $37.37. Their $54.44 for 2027 needs the margin to recover. On the third-quarter call, Goldman Sachs analyst Irma Sgarz asked whether a turn was in sight, and CFO Martin de los Santos gave no target: "The approach is to manage for the long term."

Mastercard's numbers are steadier. It trades at about 28x forward earnings, below its 31x quarter-end average since 2014. Analysts expect $23.13 of EPS for 2027, and that figure barely moved after the third-quarter beat.

Visa, at about 27x, sits right at its 28x average. The $15.02 of fiscal 2027 EPS analysts expect is at the top of Visa's guided range and only 4% above the $14.47 they expected a year ago, so there's little room for a miss.

Mastercard is the add to follow

The risk with Mastercard is what it costs to win business. Rebates and incentives rose 18% in the third quarter, and Mastercard expects them to take a larger share of its fees in the fourth.

Even so, if I could only follow one of these adds, it'd be Mastercard. Its estimates and targets are rising, and it still trades below its usual multiple. MercadoLibre has far more upside on paper, and a margin recovery would make it the better buy, but I'd want to see its estimates stop falling first.

The fund's next 13F is due in mid-February and will show whether it kept adding to MercadoLibre as the stock fell. Before that, MercadoLibre's fourth-quarter report early next year is the test. Its CFO said part of the new fulfillment costs should "come back in Q4." An operating margin back toward the 10.1% of a year earlier would make 2027's estimates look reachable again.

Shares of MercadoLibre (NASDAQ: MELI) were recently trading for about $1,427 apiece -- very close to their 52-week low of $1,418. The shares have dropped in value by about 30% over the past year (as of Nov. 17) -- though they've averaged annual gains of 20.6% over the past 15 years.

Many investors, seeing such a big drop in a stock's price, will steer clear, assuming there's trouble afoot. Others will take a closer look to see if the lower price is actually an enticing opportunity.

MercadoLibre is home to both a dominant online marketplace (Mercado Libre) and a major fintech business (Mercado Pago), both focused on the Latin American market. It's active in 18 countries and was recently delivering 3.2 billion items annually. It sports 136 million unique buyers and 93 million monthly active users (both numbers as of the third quarter). And it's growing briskly, with net revenue recently up about tenfold since 2020.

So what's going on that would depress the stock? Well, there are some concerns, such as:

Competition has been growing in the fintech realm.

The e-commerce side of the business is potentially facing more competition, too, from outside retail giants.

Geopolitical tensions in Latin America, such as in Brazil, might destabilize the business -- as the more business-friendly candidate didn't win the presidential election.

Profit margins have been shrinking.

Those are legitimate concerns, but they aren't deal-breakers. As MercadoLibre notes, it has built a powerful ecosystem, combining "the region's largest e-commerce platform, its fastest and most reliable logistics network, one of its biggest digital banks, its largest fintech payments processor, and a top-3 digital ads platform -- with a loyalty scheme that ties it all together." That's not easy to compete against.

Meanwhile, the shrinking profit margins are partly due to the company extending more free shipping and credit to shoppers and investing in future growth, such as by expanding its fulfillment capabilities. If I weren't already a shareholder, I'd consider MercadoLibre for my portfolio.

The best stocks don't just beat the market for a year or two. They compound wealth for a decade or more, and that kind of return almost always traces back to a business that keeps growing its customer base, revenue, and profits.

MercadoLibre (NASDAQ:MELI) and Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) have both delivered monster returns, and their businesses are still growing, making them quality stocks to hold for 10 years.

Missed Nvidia in 2009? This Rare Signal Is Flashing Again. In 2009, a "Double Down" signal flashed for a little-known chipmaker called Nvidia. For the first time in years, that same "Total Conviction" signal is flashing for a company 1/100th the size of Nvidia. Continue »

1. MercadoLibre

A $10,000 investment in MercadoLibre 10 years ago would be worth about $94,000 today, a roughly 25% annualized return. However, the stock trades more than 40% below its June 2025 high because profits have stalled.

That is a deliberate choice, as management is prioritizing investments to strengthen the business for long-term growth. Management has lowered Brazil's free-shipping threshold several times since 2017, while ramping up credit card issuance and expanding fulfillment space nearly 20% last quarter.

It's short-term pain for long-term gain. Operating margin fell to 6.3% from 9.8% a year ago, even as revenue climbed 45% year over year. On the Nov. 4, 2026, earnings call, CEO Ariel Szarfsztejn said the company has "accepted a lower margin" to deepen customer relationships.

Those relationships are showing up in other metrics. Gross merchandise volume (GMV) rose 38% to $23 billion, unique active buyers grew 22% to 93.9 million, and purchase frequency hit a record.

The risk is that competition from Shopee and others keeps profits down longer than investors expect. Still, the economics are improving. Brazil's cost per shipment is down 14% since Q1 2025, and high-margin advertising grew 58%.

Analysts expect earnings per share (EPS) to jump 45% to $52.62 in 2027, according to Yahoo! Finance. At $1,491 as of Nov. 13, 2026, the stock trades at 28 times that estimate. That's a fair valuation for a quality e-commerce stock with excellent long-term growth prospects.

Image source: Getty Images.

2. Amazon

A $10,000 investment in Amazon 10 years ago would be worth about $70,000 today, a roughly 22% annualized return. The engine behind those gains is growth in operating income, which reached $104 billion over the past year, up 37% year over year, excluding foreign currency effects.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is a fast-growing, high-margin business, with revenue up 39% to $46 billion last quarter, and a backlog of $578 billion. CEO Andy Jassy expects AWS to grow more than 40% in both 2027 and 2028. Amazon also plans to sell its Trainium AI chips outside AWS starting late 2027.

Today's big story: Could Nvidia Stock Fall 50%? Follow The Cash

Coupang (CPNG) stock fell 5.5% on Monday, November 16, 2026, while the S&P 500 lost 1.9%. The company issued no announcements, earnings reports or filings, and the drop came on a day the Nasdaq Composite fell 2.5%. What was moving the market that Monday, and where does Coupang fit in it?

What Happened In The Market On November 16?

Chip stocks fell, with AMD and Intel sliding ahead of two big tests for the AI trade: Nvidia's results on Tuesday and Anthropic's expected trading debut on Thursday.

Amazon had troubles of its own. It fell 3.3% on a new AI chip export rule and a Vulcan rocket failure that destroyed 40 of its Leo satellites. Amazon and Coupang are both broadline retailers that sell goods online. Coupang sells in South Korea and in Taiwan, where it runs its own last mile network. In South Korea, it is the dominant force in logistics.

Did Coupang Fall With Other Broadline Retailers?

Coupang fell with its group, but much further. Six of the eight other broadline retailers worth $2 billion or more also fell. Across all eight, the median move was a 1.3% drop, and none of them fell 5% or more. The consumer discretionary sector fund XLY lost 1.5%.

Etsy, one of Coupang's peers, fell 4.5%, while Walmart rose 0.2%. Coupang posted a larger drop than any peer, following earlier falls of 2.1% on November 11 and 4.4% on November 12.

Coupang Stock Sits Near Its One-Year Low

Coupang stock has seen three falls at least this large in the prior 365 days. Its last move this large was a 12.0% gain on November 4. That was the day after its third-quarter earnings call.

Over the past twelve months the stock lost 49.7%, while the S&P 500 returned 11.4%. Monday's close of $14.35 sits near the stock's lowest close of the past year, $13.75 on September 28, 2026. Coupang's market value is now 0.71 times its yearly sales. For the S&P 500, that ratio is 3.2.

Coupang next reports its fourth quarter of fiscal 2026. The figure to watch is the adjusted EBITDA margin of its Product Commerce segment, which management put at 4.6% for the third quarter and said it believes was the low point.

Coupang said nothing on Monday and still fell further than any of its eight sub-industry peers with a market value of $2 billion or more. Being ready for days like that matters more than trying to call them.

Investors often choose between proven global leaders and high-growth regional powerhouses. Deciding between Booking Holdings Inc. (NASDAQ:BKNG) and MercadoLibre Inc. (NASDAQ:MELI) requires weighing stable profitability against an expanding digital ecosystem in Latin America.

Booking serves the global travel market through its massive network of accommodations and flight options. MercadoLibre dominates Latin American e-commerce and digital payments, functioning as both a retailer and a bank. While both companies operate in the consumer discretionary space, they offer very different risk-reward profiles for long-term investors looking toward 2027.

The case for Booking Holdings

Booking operates a massive network of consumer-facing brands, including Booking.com, Priceline, Agoda, and OpenTable. The company focuses on its "connected trip" strategy, which aims to integrate accommodations, flights, and rental cars into a single, seamless itinerary for travelers. By managing nearly 4.7 million accommodation properties, it relies on a broad network of travel service providers that typically operate on non-exclusive terms.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached about $28.1 billion, representing roughly 8% growth compared to the prior year. The company reported net income of approximately $7.2 billion, reflecting a net margin of about 25.5%. This performance demonstrates the company's ability to generate significant profit while expanding its presence in the international travel market.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the company carries a negative debt-to-equity ratio of roughly -3.5x, indicating that its total liabilities exceed shareholder equity. The debt-to-equity ratio, which compares total debt to the equity held by shareholders, measures how a business balances its obligations against its assets. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow, which is cash flow from operations minus capital expenditures, was about $9.1 billion.

The case for MercadoLibre

MercadoLibre operates the leading commerce and fintech ecosystem in Latin America, driven by the Mercado Libre marketplace and its Mercado Pago payment platform. As a leader among consumer discretionary stocks in its region, it relies on a vast network of third-party sellers and logistics partners. Its integrated strategy combines retail, lending, and asset management to serve over 136 million unique buyers.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached about $38.5 billion, marking about 47% growth over the previous period. The company reported net income of approximately $1.9 billion, resulting in a net margin of roughly 4.9%. This rapid top-line expansion highlights the scaling nature of its integrated digital services across major markets like Brazil and Mexico.

Today's big story: Anthropic IPO: Priced For 2031, Or 2036?

Carvana sells used cars online, and it lends many of its buyers the money to pay for them. Last quarter it sold 217,385 cars, 39% more than a year earlier. Its sales over the last 12 months reached $27.5 billion, up 50%.

Analysts expect sales to grow another 27% next year. That would be faster than every Consumer Discretionary company worth more than $50 billion except MercadoLibre. Yet 14 of those 21 companies cost more than Carvana per dollar of sales, from Amazon to McDonald's. Carvana's market value is 2.9 times its sales. Three things explain that low price: the yardstick, the stock's fall in 2022, and car loans.

Is Carvana Really Cheap?

Only per dollar of sales. Selling a car brings in a lot of money but leaves a thin profit. Over the last 12 months, Carvana kept 19 cents per dollar of sales after the cost of the cars. It kept 8.7 cents of operating profit, what is left after all running costs. McDonald's kept 46.1 cents of operating profit per dollar.

On operating profit, Carvana's market value is 32.7 times, more than investors pay for Home Depot or McDonald's. Carvana has two classes of shares, and its market value here counts both.

Why Won't Investors Pay Up For The Growth?

MercadoLibre: Maintaining a Steady Upward Revenue Expansion

MercadoLibre (NASDAQ:MELI) primarily earns its revenue by operating a prominent digital commerce marketplace alongside a complementary financial technology platform that facilitates secure digital transactions and credit services for users across the broader Latin American region.

While managing a planned leadership transition for its global chief executive officer position, it successfully completed a $1 billion issuance of senior unsecured notes to institutional investors and expanded its marketplace delivery and pharmacy capabilities across Brazil.

Shopify: Experiencing Seasonal Spikes in Revenue Trends

Shopify (NASDAQ:SHOP) generates its revenue by providing an extensive digital commerce technology platform that equips independent global merchants with the necessary software tools to build digital storefronts, manage inventory, and fulfill their merchandise sales.

While navigating a California federal judge's recent refusal to dismiss a class action lawsuit regarding consumer data collection, it rolled out an extensive software update featuring new artificial intelligence integrations designed specifically for various merchant store checkouts.

Why Revenue Matters for Investors

Revenue here refers to the data provider's standardized income-statement revenue line item, and it functions as a primary financial measure that allows investors to track the overall monetary volume of goods and services a business successfully sells to its customer base.
